questions.q: If the data ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots {x}_{10}$ is such that the mean of first four of these is $11,$ the mean of the remaining six is $16$ and the sum of squares of all of these is $2000$, then the standard deviation of this data is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the numbers are ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots {x}_{10} \left(N = 10\right)$
Given \left
{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + {x}_{3} + {x}_{4} = 4.11 = 44
{x}_{5} + {x}_{6} \ldots . + {x}_{10} = 6.16 = 96
\right\} ⇒ ∑ {x}_{i} = 140$
$⇒$ variance ${σ}^{2} = $\dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{N} - $\left(\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{N})2$
$⇒ {σ}^{2} = \dfrac{2000}{10} - \left(\dfrac{140}{10}\right)$2$
$⇒ {σ}^{2} = 200 - 196 = 4$
$⇒$~Standard deviation $\sigma =2 .$

questions.q: Let the mean of& $50$ observations is $15$~and the standard deviation is $2$. However, one observation was wrongly recorded. The sum of the correct and incorrect observations is $70$. If the mean of the correct set of observations is $16$, then the variance of the correct set is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
By using the formula of& mean we get,& $= \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{50} = 15 ⇒ ∑ {x}_{i} = 750$

Now variance$= \dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{50} - {15}^{2} = {2}^{2} ⇒ ∑ {x}_i^{2} = 11450$

$⇒ \mathop{∑ {x}_{i}}_{new} = 50 \times 16 = 800$

So,~$\mathop{∑ {x}_{i}}_{new} - ∑ {x}_{i} = 800 - 750 = 50$

Hence, if wrong observation was $x$~then corrected one is~$x + 50$.
$⇒ x + \left(x + 50\right) = 70 ⇒ x = 10$

Therefore, the correct observation~$= 60$.

Now,~$\mathop{∑ {xi}^{2}}_{new} = 11450 - \left(10\right)2 + \left(60\right)2 = 14950$

Therefore,~variance of the correct set~$= \dfrac{14950}{50} - \left(16\right)2 = 299 - 256 = 43$.

questions.q: Let the mean of 6 observations $1, 2, 4, 5, x$ and $y$ be $5$ and their variance be $10$. Then their mean deviation about the mean is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Consider the data& $1, 2, 4, 5, x, y$.

So,

$Mean = \dfrac{1 + 2 + 4 + 5 + x + y}{6}$

$⇒ 5 = \dfrac{x + y + 12}{6}$

$⇒ x + y = 18$

And,

$Variance = \left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{}{x}_i^{2}}{n}\right) - \left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{}{x}_{i}}{n}\right)2$

$⇒ 10 = \left(\dfrac{{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + {4}^{2} + {5}^{2} + x^{2} + y^{2}}{6}\right) - \left(5\right)2$

$⇒ x^{2} + y^{2} = 164$

We have~$x + y = 18$~and~$x^{2} + y^{2} = 164$.

Now solving above equations we get,~$x = 10, y = 8$,

Now mean deviation about mean will be~$= \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{6}\left|{x}_{i} - x\right|}{6}$

$= \dfrac{\left|1 - 5\right| + \left|2 - 5\right| + \left|4 - 5\right| + \left|5 - 5\right| + \left|10 - 5\right| + \left|8 - 5\right|}{6}$

$= \dfrac{16}{6}$

$= \dfrac{8}{3}$

Therefore, the required answer is~$\dfrac{8}{3}$

questions.q: Consider $10$ observation ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, . .. {x}_{10}$, such that $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - \alpha\right) = 2$ and $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - \beta\right)2 = 40$, where $\alpha, \beta$ are positive integers. Let the mean and the variance of the observations be $\dfrac{6}{5}$ and $\dfrac{84}{25}$ respectively. The $\dfrac{β}{α}$ is equal to:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given observations are ${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, . . . , {x}_{10}$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - \alpha\right) = 2$

$⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}{x}_{i} - 10\alpha = 2$

Mean, $\mu = \dfrac{6}{5} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{10}$

$⇒ ∑ {x}_{i} = 12$

$⇒ 10\alpha + 2 = 12$

$⇒ \alpha = 1$

Now, $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - \beta\right)2 = 40$. Let ${y}_{i} = {x}_{i} - \beta$

$⇒ {σ}_y^{2} = \dfrac{1}{10} ∑ {y}_i^{2} - \left(\overset{¯}{y}\right)2$

$⇒ \dfrac{84}{25} = \dfrac{1}{10} ∑ \left({x}_{i} - \beta\right)2 - \left(\dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{10}\left({x}_{i} - \beta\right)}{10}\right)2$

$⇒ \dfrac{84}{25} = 4 - \left(\dfrac{12 - 10\beta}{10}\right)2$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{6 - 5\beta}{5}\right)2 = 4 - \dfrac{84}{25}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{6 - 5\beta}{5}\right)2 = \dfrac{16}{25}$

$⇒ 6 - 5\beta = \pm 4$

$⇒ \beta = \dfrac{2}{5}$ (not possible) or $\beta = 2$

Hence, $\dfrac{β}{α} = 2$

questions.q:
If $\mathop{Σ}_{i = 1}^{n}\left({x}_{i} - a\right) = n$ and $\mathop{Σ}_{i = 1}^{n} \left({x}_{i} -a\right)2 = na, \left($n, a > 1\right)$, then the standard deviation of $n$ observations~${x}_{1}, {x}_{2}, \ldots , {x}_{n}$ is
& $
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
SD,& $\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{n} - \left(\dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{n}\right)2}$

SD is independent of change of origin, so, for given data
$\sigma = \sqrt{\dfrac{Σ\left({x}_{i} - a\right)2}{n} - \left(\dfrac{Σ\left({x}_{i} - a\right)}{n}\right)2}$
$= \sqrt{\dfrac{na}{n} - \left(\dfrac{n}{n}\right)2} = \sqrt{a - 1}$

questions.q: The number of values of $a \in N$ such that the variance of $3, 7, 12, a, 43 - a$ is a natural number is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Calculating Mean& $= \dfrac{3 + 7 + 12 + a + 43 - a}{5} = 13$

Variance~$= \dfrac{9 + 49 + 144 + a^{2} + \left(43 - a\right){}^{2}}{5} - {13}^{2} \in N$

$⇒ \dfrac{2a^{2} - a + 1}{5} = n$~(where $n \in N$)

$⇒ 2a^{2} - a + 1 - 5n = 0$~must have solution as~natural numbers

So,~$D = 40n - 7$~always has $3$ at unit place for any value of~$n$

$⇒ D$~can't be perfect square

So, $a$& can't be integer.

questions.q: Let the mean and standard deviation of marks of class A of $100$~students be respectively $40$ and $\alpha  \left(> 0\right)$, and the mean and standard deviation of marks of class $B$ of $n$ students be respectively $55$ and $30 - \alpha.$If the mean and variance of the marks of the combined class of $100 + n$ students are respectively $50$ and $350$ , then the sum of variances of classes $A$ and $B is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let the mean is denoted by& $\overset{¯}{xi}$, variance by~${\sigmai}^{2}$, so standard deviation will be~${σ}_{i}$,~now as per given data we get,

$\begin{cases}A & & B & & A + B \\ \overset{¯}{x}1 = 40 & & \overset{¯}{x}2 = 55 & & \overset{¯}{x} = 50 \\ {σ}_{1} = \alpha & & {σ}_{2} = 30 - \alpha & & {σ}_{2} = 350 \\ {n}_{1} = 100 & & {n}_{2} = n & & 100 + n\end{cases}$

So, using the formula of mean in~$A + B$~we get,

$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{100 \times 40 + 55n}{100 + n} = 50$

$⇒ n = 200$

Now using the formula~of variance we get,

${σ}_{1}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{100} - {40}^{2} = {α}^{2}$

And~${σ}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {y}_i^{2}}{200} - {55}^{2} = \left(30 - \alpha\right)2$

So, variance of~$A + B$~will be,

${σ}^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2} + ∑ {y}_i^{2}}{300} - {50}^{2} = {350}^{2}$

$⇒ {350}^{2} = \dfrac{\left(1600 + {α}^{2}\right) \times 100 + \left[3025 + \left(30 - \alpha\right)2\right] \times 200}{300} - {50}^{2}$

$⇒ {α}^{2} - 40\alpha + 300 = 0$

$⇒ \alpha = 10$~or $30$

And~$\alpha = 30$~is not possible

So,~${σ}_{1} + 2 {σ}_{2} = 2 {10}^{2} + {20}^{2} = 500$

questions.q: For a statistical data $\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{x}_2, \ldots, \mathrm{x}_{10}$ of 10 values, a student obtained the mean as 5.5 and $\sum_{i=1}^{10} x_i^2=371$. He later found that he had noted two values in the data incorrectly as 4 and 5 , instead of the correct values 6 and 8 , respectively. The variance of the corrected data is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Mean } \overline{\mathrm{x}}=5.5 \\ & =\sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{10} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}=5.5 \times 10=55 \\ & =\sum_{\mathrm{i}=1}^{10} \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2=371 \\ & \left(\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}\right)_{\text {new }}=55-(4+5)+(6+8)=60 \\ & \\ & \left(\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2\right)_{\text {new }}=371-\left(4^2+5^2\right)+\left(6^2+8^2\right)=430\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \text { Variance } \sigma^2=\frac{\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}^2}{10}-\left(\frac{\sum \mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{i}}}{10}\right)^2 \\ & \sigma^2=\frac{430}{10}-\left(\frac{60}{10}\right)^2 \\ & \sigma^2=43-36 \\ & \sigma^2=7\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Let in a series of $2n$ observations, half of them~are equal to $a$ and remaining half are equal to~$- a$. Also by adding a constant $b$ in each of these observations, the mean and standard deviation~of new set become $5$ and $20$, respectively. Then~the value of $a^{2} + b^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Let observations are denoted by $xi$ for $1 \le i < 2n$

$\overset{¯}{x} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_{i}}{2n} = \dfrac{( a + a + \ldots + a ) - ( a + a + \ldots + a )}{2n}$

$⇒ \overset{¯}{x} = 0$

and ${σ}_x^{2} = \dfrac{∑ {x}_i^{2}}{2n} - \left(\overset{¯}{x}\right)2 = \dfrac{a^{2} + a^{2} + \ldots + a^{2}}{2n} - 0 = a^{2}$

$⇒ {σ}_{x} = a$

Now, adding a constant $b$ then $\overset{¯}{y} = \overset{¯}{x} + b = 5$

$⇒ b = 5$

and ${σ}_{y} = {σ}_{x}$ (No change in S.D.)~ $⇒ a = 20$

$⇒ a^{2} + b^{2} = 425$

questions.q: The mean age of $25$ teachers in a school is $40$ years. A teacher retires at the age of $60$ years and a new teacher is appointed in his place. If the mean age of the teachers in this school now is $39$ years, then the age (in years) of the newly appointed teacher is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Mean age can be calculated as

$\overset{-}{x} = \dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + \ldots {x}_{25}}{25} = 40$

$⇒{x}_{1} + {x}_{2} + \ldots + {x}_{25} = 1000$

Let age of new teacher be A, then

$1000 - 60 + A = 39 \times 25 = 975$

$⇒A = 975 - 940 = 35$
